# v2.69

This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases **v2.68-dev** and **v2.69-dev**. It covers
two areas: forward-looking compliance projection on Compliance Planning, and a set of
correctness fixes to Data Clean-Up's suggested name fixes.

---

## Compliance Planning — the renewal window now shows what it breaks

Picking a **Renewal window** on **Programs → Compliance Planning** was easy to miss: you
got a small `▼13` marker and a list of people, while the requirement itself still showed a
green tick, a green *have / need*, and a green **Achieved** badge. A requirement sitting at
`16 / 5` with 13 holders expiring inside the window looked perfectly healthy — even though
it lands at `3 / 5` and drops out of compliance.

Selecting a window now projects compliance forward, using the same treatment as the program
dashboards' **Compliance as of**:

- Attained figures read **current → projected** (`16 → 3`) with a **▼N expiring** note under
  the number, where it belongs.
- Anything met **today** that falls below target by the end of the window is shaded **amber**
  and badged **"At risk in 12mo"** right next to its green **Achieved** badge — compliant
  now, not compliant then. The Gap column spells it out: *✓ now · need 2 in 12mo*.
- An at-risk specialisation is **expanded by default**, so the numbers behind the warning are
  on screen instead of hidden inside a collapsed card.
- The headline stops saying "fully compliant — nobody left to certify" when the window says
  otherwise.
- **Renewals at risk** now opens with a summary of exactly which requirements the expiries
  break — e.g. *Cert A or Cert B: 16 → 3 / 5 (Region R)* — instead of only listing people.
- A banner at the top explains the colour coding whenever a window is selected.

### New: "Plan for this window"

By default the window is informational — the KPIs and **Who to certify** still answer *what
is broken today*. Tick the new **Plan for this window** checkbox beside the window selector
to fold it into the plan:

- Gaps are sized from the projected figure, so **People to certify** now includes the
  renewals needed to hold compliance through the window (with an *incl. N renewals* hint).
- Those people appear in **Who to certify** as a new cheapest-ranked **Renewal (expiring)**
  candidate type, with a plain-language explanation: *"They hold Cert A, but it expires
  within the renewal window. Renewing it keeps the Specialisation Y specialisation
  compliant."*
- For a tiered program this can change which specialisations are **Recommended** — one that
  lapses inside the window no longer counts toward the tier.

The checkbox is disabled (and cleared) when the window is **Off**.

### Exports

With a window selected, the **Export report** roadmap gains **Projected (+Nmo)**,
**Expiring**, **Projected gap** and **Projected achieved** columns, a **Requirements at
risk** section is included, and the file name carries a `-plusNmo` suffix (plus `-planned`
when planning for the window). The summary sheet distinguishes *renewals at risk* (holders
expiring) from *renewals included in plan* so the two aren't read as additive.

---

## Data Clean-Up no longer suggests fixes that create new problems

Scanning student names on **Admin → Data Clean-Up** could offer a "fix" that swapped one
issue for another. A learner recorded as `Jane Jane` with the address `jane11.jane@co.com`
was offered **`Jane11 Jane`** — the duplicate was resolved, but the digits from the email
came along for the ride, and the very next scan flagged the result as a **Numbers** issue.
Applying the fix wrote a visibly wrong name to the database and only settled down after a
second pass.

Names rebuilt from an email address are now cleaned properly:

- **Digits are stripped** — `jane11.jane@co.com` no longer contributes `Jane11`.
- **Plus-addressing tags are dropped** — `jane.doe+hr@co.com` gives `Jane Doe`, not
  `Jane Doehr` (which the scanner used to re-flag as a special character).
- When the email offers nothing better than the duplicate you started with, the suggestion
  is simply the de-duplicated name: `Jane Jane` → `Jane`.

**No suggested fix can be re-flagged any more.** That's now a property the whole feature is
built around, rather than something each rule handled separately.

### Other fixes in the same area

- **A fuller name is only taken from the email when it belongs to the same person.** A
  shared or mis-keyed mailbox could previously rewrite someone's name to a *different*
  person's — and because the result looked clean, nothing ever flagged it.
- **Initials are no longer treated as duplicates.** `J R R Smith` was flagged as a duplicate
  name and is now left alone.
- **Accented and non-Latin names are safe.** Combining marks — Devanagari matras, decomposed
  accents, Arabic pointing — were being flagged as special characters and *deleted*, silently
  corrupting the name. A typographic apostrophe is now converted rather than removed
  (`O’Brien` → `O'Brien`, not `OBrien`). Note that names already "fixed" under the old
  behaviour have lost those marks and now look clean, so a fresh scan will not find them.
- **Deliberate capitalisation survives.** Casing is corrected only for names that are
  entirely upper- or lower-case, so `McDonald` and `van der Berg` are no longer flattened by
  a fix for something unrelated.
- **Suggestions that would change nothing are no longer offered.** The field is left blank
  with a prompt to enter a name, and the row can't be selected until you do.
- **Repeated internal spaces are now detected**, under the existing Spaces issue.

### Selection and reliability

- The **Fix Selected** count now always matches the number of records actually updated.
  Editing a suggestion to blank after ticking its box used to leave it in the request.
- **Select All** correctly flips to **Deselect All** again.
- Failed scans and failed fixes now show an error instead of silently doing nothing — an
  expired session previously just stopped the spinner with no explanation.
- Fixes are applied in a single transaction, and reports refresh immediately afterwards
  rather than showing the old names for up to 30 seconds.

### Imports

Student import shared the same name-building code, and the same problems. It also used to
write the **whole email address** into the Full Name field when the local part wasn't
exactly `first.last` — creating the "Email as Name" issue that the clean-up page exists to
fix. Both now use one shared implementation, so imported names come out as `Jsmith` or
`First Middle Last` rather than a raw address, `o'brien` becomes `O'Brien`, and stray double
spaces are collapsed on the way in.
